prompt: Complete an immutable Point3D class: translate(dx, dy, dz) must return a brand-new Point3D and leave the original untouched, and toString must format the point as "(x, y, z)".
explanation: Because the fields are final, the only way translate can produce a moved point is to construct and return a new Point3D -- this is the immutable object pattern used by java.time and String. Immutability makes objects safe to share and to use as map keys, since no caller can change them behind your back. Chaining works naturally because each call returns a fresh instance.
hints: Final fields cannot be reassigned, so translate must call the constructor with new coordinate values.
The new coordinates are x + dx, y + dy, and z + dz.
For toString, concatenate the parts: "(" + x + ", " + y + ", " + z + ")".
